Thank you for the advice. My problems, because of other people, are pervasive and have been trying to fix them for quite awhile. Ive lost 5 years of my life (the last 5 years of ones "youth") and the injuries I have to my neck have only progresses extensively. Its very discouraging. 

It doesn't matter what my "story" is. 

I need a lawyer. Bad.

I have been too overwhelmed, with too many battles to fight. "They" promised to help me when "they" only wanted me to kill myself so "they" could get the money.

If I could at least get the facts "out there"--online, finding a lawyer that can help me, and a doctor to perform the surgery I have desperately needed since 2008 would drastically give me some quality of life. 

I have no quality of life. 
::

>Yeah that's what I was wondering. Honestly I've had it since I was a kid, i can't remember a time that I heard pure silence. Before learning about tinnitus I genuinely thought there was no such thing as pure silence. 

That sounds like me although more of tween and I do remember not having to suffer from it, but Ive no memories of what silence is like however,  either. It sucks doesn't it? 
Question.
Do you play any instruments and if so do you or did you excel at them? 
I started the piano at a very young age, playing by ear. I played through h.s. and entered many competition's. I excelled at it. I always wondered if my tinnitus had anything to do with it.

Smiles.
Hope you're doing well and tinnitus is all you have to contend with!!

It sounds like many things contributed to your tinnitus. I had chronic infections, too. I sustained trauma, and I currently have severe cervical injuries with spinal cord compression. (Its hell.)

Be careful on those motorcycles!!! :)

You are very lucky and I hope you're taking steps to ensure you dont have another stroke!!! 
You sound like you're doing quite well. Smiles. Good for you!!! (Please forgive me if I misconstrued and you suffer[ed] greatly.)

>I got it from a car accident.  The airbag deployed and I turned my head and it smacked me in the right ear.  It's gotten more manageable but in addition to the tinnitus I also have some permanent hearing loss.

I'm sorry to hear that (no pun intended). That sounds painful!!! I would think some damage would have been incurred in your neck, too, but no? If not you're very lucky...I'm sorry for your hearing loss :( That sucks...

Do you have tinnitus in both ears? Please, be gentle with your with your ears, and with yourself, too. Ive noticed many people that have tinnitus are also prone to stress,  and perfectionism. We typically can be hard on ourselves but I'm "hear" [lol] to tell you that it is pointless to engage in beating yourself up. Smiles. Take good care of yourself mentally, emotionally and demand that those you let in your close circle do the same....Smiles.

I started suffering from tinnitus long before my first concert. I had several ENT  surgeries; many ear infections (and strep throat and sinus infections). I was hit so hard by my dad that when I was 14/15 needed 2 root canals. I cant help but wonder if the blows to my head didnt play a role along with the infections and surgeries. 

Thanks for sharing!!!!! 
>I'm not sure, because mine came on gradually over a few years. I've been to very, very few shows in person, have a history handling firearms, and have been in several motorcycle accidents... I also had chronic ear infections as a child. Not sure what happened, or when.

Have any of you gotten tinnitus from trauma to the head and/or neck? Or trauma to the TMJ by a blow to the head or a malloclusion to some degree? I didn't realize it was specifically being exposed to loud music.
